numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Subtracting two Timestamp objects whose int64 difference equals the NaT sentinel (iNaT / INT64_MIN) raises AssertionError from the bare assert value != NPY_NAT in _timedelta_from_value_and_reso; under python -O it returns a live Timedelta whose _value is -9223372036854775808 (iNaT), with pd.isna(res) False and res is not pd.NaT.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Raise OutOfBoundsDatetime (message 'Result is too large for pandas.Timedelta. ...' style, same as the difference one step further out of bounds) instead of AssertionError or a corrupt Timedelta.
trigger_conditions: Timestamp - Timestamp where the difference of the two Timestamps' _value equals iNaT (INT64_MIN)
Running without -O raises AssertionError; running under python -O yields a corrupt Timedelta instead

input_output_examples.buggy_output: AssertionError (without -O); under python -O: Timedelta('-106752 days +00:12:43.145224192') with _value -9223372036854775808, pd.isna False
OutOfBoundsDatetime: Result is too large for pandas.Timedelta. ...

oracle_clues: Fix adds explicit check res_value == NPY_NAT raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta, which is caught and re-raised as OutOfBoundsDatetime in the enclosing except clause
Under python -O, pd.isna(res) must be True for a NaT result; the buggy output reports False
Changelog states expected result is OutOfBoundsDatetime (issue GH#66552)

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Difference of Timestamp _value equal to iNaT (INT64_MIN, -9223372036854775808); example Timestamp(iNaT + 1) - Timestamp(1) lands exactly on the sentinel
category_specific_evidence: The difference of two Timestamps lands exactly on iNaT (INT64_MIN), which fits in int64 but is not representable as a Timedelta.
Before the fix, Timestamp(iNaT + 1) - Timestamp(1) raised a bare AssertionError from assert value != NPY_NAT in _timedelta_from_value_and_reso.
Under python -O the assert vanishes and the result is a live Timedelta with _value -9223372036854775808 (iNaT), for which pd.isna(res) is False and res is not pd.NaT.
Expected behaviour after the fix: raise OutOfBoundsDatetime ("Result is too large"), the same as Timestamp(iNaT + 1) - Timestamp(2), which is one step further out of bounds.
Test test_sub_lands_on_nat_sentinel_raises parametrizes units s, ms, us, ns and asserts left._value - right._value == iNaT and OutOfBoundsDatetime on left - right and left.to_datetime64() - right.
Assertion in _timedelta_from_value_and_reso is left in place because it is still reachable from Timedelta.__mul__/__truediv__ (GH-66552, separate scope).
reproduction_risks: Behaviour differs between normal and python -O runs, since the original failure relies on the assert being stripped.
Scope is limited to Timestamp - Timestamp; Timedelta.__mul__/__truediv__ paths and the rest of GH-66552 remain open and unaddressed.
Exception-type decision for other paths (bare OverflowError on scalar vs OutOfBoundsTimedelta on TimedeltaIndex) is unresolved in the passages.
